key_insight: PING embeds advection–diffusion physics in a graph neural network to forecast transport on irregular sensor networks and improve solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better intra-day PV production forecasts can support grid integration of solar generation without changing solar cell hardware.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on an irregular graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-sensor data and satellite-derived cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic transport, sea surface temperature, and cloud index datasets, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting with the hybrid approach.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify PV forecasting gains, leaving their magnitude and operational significance unclear.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
